title: Poems from the Divan of Hafiz
author: Hafiz (Gertrude Bell trans)
description: Poems from the Divan of Hafiz, translated by Gertrude Lowthian Bell (London: William Heinemann, 1897), with introduction and notes. Hafiz of Shiraz (Shams al-Din Muhammad, c. 1315-1390) is the supreme master of the Persian ghazal, and his Divan has been revered for six centuries as a guide to the mystical life and used for divination. Bell, later famous as an archaeologist, traveller and political officer in the Middle East, translated forty-three ghazals into English verse after studying Persian in Tehran. The poems celebrate wine, the beloved, the rose and the nightingale, the tavern and the inspired libertine, against the hypocrisy of the pious, in imagery that can be read both as earthly love and as Sufi symbolism of divine love and intoxication. Bell's long introduction on Hafiz's life and age is admired, and her translation is still considered among the finest in English.
